name: STING Tag Token Policy — corporate baseline
description: Per-token completeness policy for the ISO 19650 tag. Corporate baseline; override per project at <project>/_BIM_COORD/tag_token_policy.json. This is DATA, not code, because sectors disagree — a hospital treats ZONE as mandatory (fire compartment), a single-building lodge does not.
_readBy: TagTokenPolicyRegistry.Get(doc) -> TagTokenPolicy.Resolve, called from TagConfig.BuildAndWriteTag for DISC/LOC/ZONE/LVL/SYS/FUNC/PROD. From 2026-08-10 until 2026-09-15 this file was read by NOTHING: the fallbacks were hardcoded literals in TagConfig and editing this file changed no behaviour.
_refusal: A token whose fallback is null and whose level is not OPTIONAL is REFUSED: the element is skipped, counted in the tagging result as REFUSED, and no tag is written. Every one of the seven tag segments ships WITH a fallback, so the shipped baseline never refuses — only a project override can turn that on.
_notYetGoverned: LOC and ZONE are substituted upstream of the policy (TagConfig ~line 2355 uses LocCodes/ZoneCodes from project_config.json), so for those two the policy fallback VALUE is only reached if that upstream guard does not fire. Their level is honoured; their fallback value may not be. See ROADMAP TOKPOL-1.
_model: K-13 classified the sixteen ISO sheet tokens into fallback-to-profile / omit-and-fail-loud / blank-is-safe. This applies the same grouping to the ten tag tokens, and reuses G-27's Empty vs Unmatched distinction rather than inventing a second vocabulary.

levels.MANDATORY: Never blank. A blank is an error: it is counted, surfaced in the tagging result, and the element is reported as incomplete.
levels.DERIVED: May fall back, but the fallback is RECORDED — the tag is complete-but-assumed, which is not the same as complete (G-27's Empty).

tokens.why: An asset with no discipline cannot be routed, scheduled or filed. Every downstream ISO surface keys on it.

G-41: on a project with no declared LOC codes this silently became EXT on elements INSIDE a building. Falling back is acceptable; doing it silently is not. Warn once per document naming the parameter and where to declare it.
The token most likely to be overridden per sector. Healthcare and fire-strategy work should raise this to MANDATORY in the project override; a single-building lodge should not.

Every model element sits on a level, so a blank is a defect — but GetLevelCode returns "XX" for a genuinely levelless element (a nested component, a group), and L00 is the encoding of that. MANDATORY here means the substitution is counted and surfaced SEPARATELY from the DERIVED ones, not that it is refused. Set this to null to refuse instead: a levelless element is then skipped and counted rather than tagged L00. Before 2026-09 the L00 substitution was a hardcoded literal that recorded nothing.
Architectural elements legitimately have no MEP system. GEN is a real answer for them, not a guess.

G-39: the air terminal's System Type read 'Undefined', so the system-aware lookup had no key. FUNC is derived FROM SYS, so when SYS itself is a fallback, FUNC cannot be better than one — failing loud here would fail every architectural element. Recorded as assumed instead.
Resolved through ProdMap and family-aware rules. A GEN fallback is visible and correctable; blocking would stop tagging on any un-catalogued family.

G-40: a tag ending in a bare separator is ALWAYS wrong. SEQ is what makes the tag unique — without it the tag is not an identifier. There is no defensible fallback. SEQ never reaches the policy: SeqAssigner.AssignNext generates it and already returns false (element skipped, counter rolled back) on overflow or collision exhaustion, which is this rule enforced one layer earlier.
tokens.governedNote: Generated by SeqAssigner.AssignNext, which never returns an empty value and already skips the element on overflow or collision exhaustion — this rule enforced one layer earlier. The entry is documentation of that contract, not a rule TagTokenPolicy.Resolve evaluates.

tokens.why: Not part of the 8-segment tag; carried for lifecycle reporting.
tokens.governedNote: Not part of the 8-segment tag string, so BuildAndWriteTag never resolves it through the policy. Carried for lifecycle reporting. The entry documents the intent; nothing reads it.

tokens.why: Not part of the 8-segment tag; blank before first issue is correct.
tokens.governedNote: Not part of the 8-segment tag string, so BuildAndWriteTag never resolves it through the policy. The entry documents the intent; nothing reads it.

_governance: Seven of the ten tokens are resolved through TagTokenPolicy.Resolve from TagConfig.BuildAndWriteTag: DISC LOC ZONE LVL SYS FUNC PROD. The other three carry governedByResolve=no and a governedNote saying why. Before 2026-09-16 the file read as if all ten were governed, which is the same over-claim the file itself was guilty of when NOTHING read it.
